svg.title: The arbiter's six stations, from the offers to the envelopes and the reasons
svg.desc: Predict: each row's quoted host time is corrected by what the cost book learnt of it, a little above for a row whose runs vary. Plan: the target loses a margin read from the frames' spread, and a switch of row is charged its preparation and its swap. Propose: the greedy pass and the exact search each plan one row per agent. Shield: each plan is checked against the policies, the frame's time and the memory; a refused plan is dropped. Share: the best plan accepted is lent as envelopes, the slack shared, each envelope held under the next better row and converted back into the agent's own quoted units. Journal: the decision is kept with why it was made.

g.text: shadows · medium · quoted 2.0 ms of host time
learnt: measured ≈ 1.5 × quoted, spread 0.1
The cost book corrects each row's host time by what its runs measured.
A row above the floor is planned a little higher while its runs vary;
the floor is planned at its factor alone. Other devices stay as quoted.
target 16.7 ms − margin 0.8 ms = 15.9 ms planned
switch shadows → high: 0.75 × (5 ms + 250 ms) / 5 s
charged ≈ 0.04 of weighed quality
The margin keeps the plans clear of the frames' usual spread. A switch of
row is charged its preparation and its swap, spread over the 5 s a plan
is meant to hold: an upgrade must gain more than it costs to make.

Two proposers each plan one row per agent. The greedy is quick and near
the best; the exact search starts from its plan and can only improve it.

Whatever proposed it, a plan reaches the frame only through the shield.
Of the plans accepted the arbiter keeps the one worth most; none accepted,
every agent keeps the row admission gave it.
shadows planned 3.3 ms + its part of 80 % of the slack
held under the next better row · 3.6 ms measured
lent in its own units: 3.6 ÷ 1.5 = 2.4 ms quoted
The envelope is cut just under the next better row, so the agent runs the
row planned; it is lent in the agent's quoted units, since the agent chooses
by its own quotes. 20 % of the slack stays back for spikes.
Why { by: Exact, trigger: FrameGovernor,
binding: Time(Cpu),
rejected: [audio → HighPerformance, Time(Cpu)] }
Each decision says who decided, why the round opened, what stopped the plan
growing and which upgrades were refused. The editor shows it; a journal keeps
it with every input the round read, so the round can be decided again.
